DELIVERABLE: Each event gets an event_id generated once when the event is created, and every retry resends that same event_id unchanged so merchants dedupe on it. Sign the raw request body bytes exactly as sent, together with a timestamp header, as HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp.raw_body`, and receivers reject timestamps outside a 5-minute replay window. Each event carries a per-order sequence number, and consumers discard any event whose sequence is lower than the last one they applied.
BOUNDARY: Covers the event contract only, not merchant-side storage or the retry schedule.
EVIDENCE: Replay one event three times and confirm the same event_id each time; verify the signature in Go, Node and Python against the raw bytes; deliver order.updated after order.cancelled and confirm it is dropped as stale.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Retries reuse the original event id: the id is assigned once per event, never per attempt. (2) The HMAC covers a timestamp plus the unmodified body bytes, never re-sorted JSON, with a 300 s tolerance. (3) Every event includes `version`, incremented per order; a consumer that already holds a higher version ignores the older event.
BOUNDARY: No change to which events exist.
EVIDENCE: Contract tests for duplicate delivery, cross-language signature checks, and out-of-order delivery.

DELIVERABLE: Keep a fresh uuid per delivery attempt, add exponential backoff, and sign the canonical sorted JSON so every language agrees.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

BOUNDARY: No caller is forced to migrate.
EVIDENCE: Existing call-site tests pass untouched; new tests cover each kind.

DELIVERABLE: Introduce a separate function `get_user_strict(email)` that raises `UserNotFound` or `InvalidEmail`, each carrying a stable `code`; find_user keeps returning None exactly as today.
BOUNDARY: Not redefining find_user.
EVIDENCE: Run the three services' suites unchanged.

BOUNDARY: none

DELIVERABLE: Add `"v": 2` to every new record and write new entries under a versioned key `quote:v2:<sku>`, so old workers never read them. Readers treat any record whose version they do not recognize, or that lacks a version, as a cache miss and recompute instead of parsing it.
BOUNDARY: Covers the cache record only.
EVIDENCE: During a canary overlap, old and new workers each read the other's key and recompute rather than crash.

DELIVERABLE: (1) The record gains a schema_version field. (2) For the overlap, new workers dual-write price and price_cents, so old workers keep reading price. (3) A reader that finds an unsupported schema version skips the entry and recomputes it.
BOUNDARY: No change to quote math.
EVIDENCE: Rolling-deploy test with mixed workers.

DELIVERABLE: Deploy as planned; new code reads price_cents and old code reads price, so it is fine. Use a 6 h TTL.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Every error returns {"error":{"code","message","details"}} where code is a stable machine-readable constant. Malformed JSON is 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST; end_date before start_date is 422 INVALID_DATE_RANGE; a stale revision token is 409 REVISION_CONFLICT; a non-owner is 403 FORBIDDEN; the database timeout is 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with no SQL or stack text, which is logged server-side only.
BOUNDARY: Status categories and codes only.
EVIDENCE: One contract test per failure asserting status and code.

DELIVERABLE: (1) 400 for unparseable JSON. (2) A date range where end_date precedes start_date returns 422. (3) Stale revision: 412 Precondition Failed when sent via If-Match, else 409 Conflict. (4) Authenticated non-owner: 403. (5) Timeouts: 503 or 500, and the SQL text never appears in the response. Each body carries a stable `code` clients branch on.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: tests

DELIVERABLE: Keep 400 for all failures but improve the message text so clients can parse it.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Revert the 40-line truncation: once the router activates a skill, load its entire SKILL.md, because a partial load drops the verification steps and leaves the agent with half a procedure. Reject loading skills whose description shares any word with the request; that is eager loading that recreates context stuffing. Keep the 6K-token name-and-description index and activate a skill only when the task explicitly matches its trigger.
BOUNDARY: The router and index stay as they are.
EVIDENCE: Re-run tasks that skipped verification and check the steps now run; track tokens per activated skill.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Load activated skills fully, not their first 40 lines. (2) Keep strict activation thresholds; word-overlap loading would add noise. (3) Save tokens by activating fewer skills, not by cutting each one.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: Compare completion of bottom-of-file steps before and after.

DELIVERABLE: Keep the 40-line loads and raise the cap to 60 lines; also preload skills that share words with the request so nothing is missed.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Keep the last 10 tool results in full and replace older ones with a short summary plus a path or command to re-fetch them; deleting every result as soon as the next call starts would force the agent to re-read files it still needs. EVIDENCE: Replay the 180-call tasks and count constraint violations and re-reads before and after.

BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: measure violations
